mcqNotes.18: The printed key gives C. When the ball rebounds, its final momentum is opposite its initial momentum. The magnitude of the net impulse is the sum of their magnitudes, so it exceeds the incoming momentum. The reviewed answer is D.
mcqNotes.62: The question says incident wave, but antinodes refer to the standing wave. Interpreting adjacent antinodes as half a wavelength gives the keyed 50 m/s.
mcqNotes.65: The calculation uses the printed measurements: 1000/(0.5 × 10) = 200 J/(kg·K). This is an experimental result implied by the data, not the accepted specific heat of water.
mcqNotes.33: Doppler redshift measurement is the standard astronomical method used to determine the radial recession velocity of expanding galaxies (Hubble's law). The board also accepted B (water waves) as an alternate response.
mcqNotes.38: Doppler effect applies to both sound waves (mechanical, used in sonar) and light/radio waves (electromagnetic, used in satellite tracking). The board keyed C (light and sound).
mcqNotes.46: The maximum theoretical (Carnot) efficiency of an engine operating between 1500 K and 600 K is $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \frac{600}{1500} = 60\%$.
mcqNotes.49: For an ideal gas, temperature is proportional to $PV$. The diagram gives $PV=9$ at iii, 8 at iv, 3 at ii and v, and 1 at i, so point iii alone is the hottest state. The printed option D listed “iii and v”, although v is not the hottest; D has been corrected to read “iii only.” The board key A (“ii only”) does not follow from the diagram.
mcqNotes.53: The Vernier zero lies to the left of the main-scale zero, so the zero error is negative. The keyed third-division mismatch gives $-0.03\text{ mm}$.
